heading: Liji 5 · Zengzi Wen 曾子問 · Questions Of Zang-Dze · Zengzi Wen I.26 … Zengzi Wen II.7

items.text: Do not mourn for a foster-mother as for a mother; if mourning is unavoidable, use the lesser garb of the soft inner garment and cap.
items.quote: It is not the rule to mourn for a foster-mother as for a mother.

items.text: During the three years' mourning for a parent, do not go to condole with others; let ceremonies express true feeling, not empty form.
items.quote: Would it not be an empty form to go and condole and wail with others, while wearing the three years' mourning?

heading: Liji 5 · Zengzi Wen 曾子問 · Questions Of Zang-Dze · Zengzi Wen I.8 … Zengzi Wen I.18

items.text: After being capped, sweep the ground and offer sacrifice at your father's shrine.
items.quote: he will sweep the ground, and sacrifice at his father's shrine

items.text: After being capped, present yourself before your uncles and offer proper courtesies.
items.quote: he will present himself before his uncles, and then offer the proper courtesies

items.text: Send someone to offer condolences when the parent of your betrothed dies.
items.quote: The son-in-law will send some one to condole

items.text: Offer a release from the engagement if your nephew is occupied with mourning for his parents.
items.quote: his oldest uncle will offer a release from the engagement to the lady

items.text: Agree to the release and do not insist on the marriage taking place immediately.
items.quote: it is the rule for the lady to agree to the message and not presume to (insist on) the marriage

items.text: When his mourning is concluded, send and request the fulfilment of the engagement.
items.quote: the parents of the lady will send and request (the fulfilment of the engagement)

items.text: Do not immediately carry her to your house; wait until the proper time after mourning.
items.quote: The son-in-law will not (immediately come to) carry her

items.text: When your husband's father or mother dies on the way to his house, change into mourning dress and hasten to attend the rites.
items.quote: The lady will change her dress; and in the long linen robe... will hasten to be present at the mourning rites
items.needs_role: bride on the way to her husband's house

items.text: Return to mourn your parent if they die while you are on the way to your husband's house.
items.quote: if, while she is on the way, it be her own father or mother who dies, she will return

heading: Liji 5 · Zengzi Wen 曾子問 · Questions Of Zang-Dze · Zengzi Wen I.1 … Zengzi Wen I.7

items.text: Do obeisance and wail before the coffin of your deceased father, acknowledging him as your father.
items.quote: The boy is (then made) to do obeisance, with his forehead on the ground, and to wail.
items.conflict: Conflicts with the prohibition of communication with or worship of the dead (Deut 18:10-12).

items.text: Before going to the king's court, announce your departure at your grandfather's shrine.
items.quote: must announce (their departure) before (the shrine of) their grandfather
items.conflict: Conflicts with the prohibition of communication with or worship of the dead (Deut 18:10-12).

items.text: Before going to the king's court, lay offerings at your father's shrine.
items.quote: lay their offerings in that of their father
items.conflict: Conflicts with the prohibition of communication with or worship of the dead (Deut 18:10-12).

items.text: Before visiting another prince, announce your departure at your father's shrine.
items.quote: must announce (their departure) before the shrine of their father
items.conflict: Conflicts with the prohibition of communication with or worship of the dead (Deut 18:10-12).

items.text: When burying both parents together, bury the mother first and the father second, and set down offerings in the reverse order.
items.quote: The rule is that the burying of the less important (mother) should have the precedence, and that of the more important (father) follow, while the offerings to them are set down in the opposite order.
items.conflict: Conflicts with the prohibition of communication with or worship of the dead (Deut 18:10-12).

items.text: Keep a wife to preside with you at funeral rites, even into old age.
items.quote: The eldest son, even though seventy, should never be without a wife to take her part in presiding at the funeral rites.
items.conflict: No biblical requirement to remarry to have a wife for rites; a widower may remain unmarried (1 Cor 7:8-9).

items.text: On returning from a journey, announce in person to your father.
items.quote: they will announce (the fact) in person to their grandfather and father
items.conflict: Conflicts with the prohibition of communication with or worship of the dead (Deut 18:10-12).

items.text: On returning from a journey, announce in person to your grandfather.
items.quote: they will announce (the fact) in person to their grandfather and father
items.conflict: Conflicts with the prohibition of communication with or worship of the dead (Deut 18:10-12).

heading: Liji 5 · Zengzi Wen 曾子問 · Questions Of Zang-Dze · Zengzi Wen II.20 … Zengzi Wen II.28

items.text: Serve as the personator of the dead in ancestral sacrifices, representing the deceased ancestor.
items.quote: there must be such a representative, who should be a grandson
items.conflict: Ancestor veneration is forbidden; worship God alone (Ex 20:3-5).

items.text: If there is no grandson, select someone of the same surname to be the personator.
items.quote: If there be no grandson, some one of the same surname should be selected for the occasion.
items.conflict: Ancestor veneration is forbidden; worship God alone (Ex 20:3-5).

items.text: Offer the dark satisfying offering to an eldest son who died prematurely, without the full sacrificial rites.
items.quote: At the auspicious sacrifice to him, there is a single bullock; but the service being to one who died prematurely, there is no presentation
items.conflict: Ancestor veneration is forbidden; worship God alone (Ex 20:3-5).

items.text: Offer the bright satisfying offering to all others who died prematurely and left no offspring, in the house of the oldest son.
items.quote: In regard to all others who have died prematurely and have left no offspring, the sacrifice is offered to them in the house of the oldest son, where the apartment is most light.
items.conflict: Ancestor veneration is forbidden; worship God alone (Ex 20:3-5).

items.text: In performing rites, do not expose your relatives to distress or danger.
items.quote: a superior man, in his performance of rites, will not expose his relatives to the risk of distress or evil.

items.text: If a relative dies in a government hotel while on official business, recall his spirit.
items.quote: the rules say that, (if he die) in a government hotel his spirit shall be recalled
items.conflict: Ancestor veneration is forbidden; worship God alone (Ex 20:3-5).

items.text: Shroud and coffin a child who dies prematurely, even if the grave is distant.
items.quote: The practice of coffins for boys who have died so prematurely, and shrouding them, began with the recorder Yî.

items.text: Do not let any duty or service rob your parents of the filial care you owe them.
items.quote: the ruler does not take from men their affection to their parents, nor do men take from their parents their filial duty.

items.text: Do not seek your own advantage by taking up official or military duties during the three years' mourning for a parent.
items.quote: I do not know if I should allow it in those who seek (by it) their own advantage during the period of the three years' mourning.

items.text: When the oldest son by the wife dies prematurely, do not let a half-brother born of an inferior wife be his successor.
items.quote: When the oldest son, who would take the father's place, dies prematurely, no brother by an inferior wife can be his successor.
items.conflict: Concubinage and the exclusion of the inferior wife's son from succession is unbiblical; marriage is monogamous (Gen 2:24).

items.text: At a burial, if the sun is eclipsed, stop the bier and wail until the eclipse passes.
items.quote: let the bier be stopped on the left of the road; and then let us wail and wait till the eclipse pass away.

items.text: Once a funeral procession has set out, do not turn it back.
items.quote: In the progress of a bier there should be no returning.

heading: Liji 5 · Zengzi Wen 曾子問 · Questions Of Zang-Dze · Zengzi Wen II.8 … Zengzi Wen II.19

items.text: After putting off mourning for the ruler, perform the great sacrificial rites for your parent.
items.quote: When the mourning for the ruler is put off, he will then perform the great sacrifices (of his private mourning).
items.conflict: Ancestor worship conflicts with the first commandment.

items.text: When your parent dies while you are engaged in the ruler's funeral, go home and remain there, attending only the ruler's great services.
items.quote: He should go home and remain there; going indeed to the ruler's for the great services, but not for those of every morning and evening.

items.text: A younger person must not pronounce a eulogy for an older person.
items.quote: nor a younger man that of one older than himself.

items.text: When your father dies abroad, receive his body home in mourning dress, entering by the proper way.
items.quote: the son in the linen cap, with the sackcloth band round it, wearing coarse sackcloth and the shoes of straw, and carrying a staff, will enter by the opening made in the wall of the apartment for the coffin, having ascended by the western steps.

items.text: If called to your parent's funeral while assisting at the ruler's, complete the lowering of the coffin, then go home without waiting for the ruler's son.
items.quote: He should complete what he is engaged in; and when the coffin has been let down into the grave, return home, without waiting for the departure of the (ruler's) son.

items.text: Complete your parent's burial before going to the ruler's funeral.
items.quote: He should complete the burial; and, when the coffin has been let down, he should change his dress, and go to (the ruler's).

items.text: As a son of a secondary wife, offer the family sacrifices in the eldest son's house, acknowledging him as head.
items.quote: He will sacrifice, with the victims belonging to his higher rank, in the house of the eldest son.
items.conflict: Ancestor worship conflicts with the first commandment.

items.text: When the eldest son is away, perform the sacrifice on his behalf, but do not take his place fully; refrain from the rites that belong only to the head.
items.quote: the principal in this vicarious service will not conduct the sacrifice so as to see that the spirit of the deceased is satisfied to the full; nor send the cup round among all who are present, nor receive the blessing (at the close); nor lay on the ground the portions of the sacrifice as thank-offerings; nor have with him (the wife of the elder brother)
items.conflict: Ancestor worship conflicts with the first commandment.

items.text: If the eldest son is away, sacrifice at an altar before the family grave; if he dies, announce it at the grave, then sacrifice in the house, but do not call yourself 'filial.'
items.quote: He will rear an altar in front of the (family-)grave, and there he will sacrifice at the different seasons. If the oldest son die, he will announce the event at the grave, and afterwards sacrifice in the house, calling himself, however, only by his name, and abstaining from the epithet 'filial.'
items.conflict: Ancestor worship conflicts with the first commandment.

heading: Liji 5 · Zengzi Wen 曾子問 · Questions Of Zang-Dze · Zengzi Wen I.19 … Zengzi Wen I.25

items.text: If a death requiring the year's or nine months' mourning occurs before the bride arrives, change your dress outside and wail with her in the proper positions.
items.quote: Before the gentleman enters, he will change his dress in a place outside. ... They will then go to the proper positions and wail.

items.text: If a death requiring the year's or nine months' mourning occurs before you arrive at his house, enter, change your dress inside, and wail with him in the proper positions.
items.quote: The lady will enter and change her dress in a place inside. They will then go to the proper positions and wail.

items.text: Do not resume the marriage ceremonies after the mourning is ended; the time has passed and cannot be recovered.
items.quote: It is the rule, that when the time of sacrifice has been allowed to pass by, it is not then offered.

items.text: Keep the candles burning for three nights after your daughter has gone away to her husband, thinking of the separation.
items.quote: The family that has married a daughter away, does not extinguish its candles for three nights, thinking of the separation that has taken place.

items.text: Have no music for three days after receiving the new wife, for her husband now takes the place of his parents.
items.quote: The family that has received the (new) wife for three days has no music; thinking her bridegroom is now in the place of his parents.

items.text: After three months present yourself in the ancestral temple and sacrifice at the shrine of your father-in-law, showing you are the established wife.
items.quote: After three months she presents herself in the ancestral temple... A day is chosen for her to sacrifice at the shrine of her father-in-law; expressing the idea of her being (now) the established wife.
items.conflict: Only God may be worshiped; ancestor veneration is forbidden (Exod 20:3-5; Deut 18:10-12).

items.text: If your wife dies before she has presented in the ancestral temple, do not carry the staff, wear straw shoes, or have a special wailing place; take her back to be buried among her own kindred, showing she was not the established wife.
items.quote: The husband should not carry the staff; nor wear the shoes of straw; nor have a (special) place (for wailing). She should be taken back, and buried among her kindred...

items.text: If death occurs before the wedding day, come to condole wearing the one year's mourning, and lay it aside when the interment has taken place.
items.quote: The son-in-law will come to condole, wearing the one year's mourning, which he will lay aside when the interment has taken place.

items.text: If your betrothed husband dies before the wedding day, condole wearing the one year's mourning and lay it aside after interment, as is done on the other side.
items.quote: If it be the husband who dies, a similar course will be followed on the other side.

items.text: In mourning rites let only one perform the part of the orphan son; in heaven there are not two suns, in a country not two kings.
items.quote: In heaven there are not two suns; in a country there are not two kings; ... there are not two who occupy the highest place of honour.

items.text: Let no shrine be left empty without its tablet; when tablets are removed, deposit them in the shrine of the high ancestor and restore each to its shrine afterwards.
items.quote: No shrine ... ought to be (left) empty. ... then every other tablet was restored to its shrine.
items.conflict: Ancestral tablets and shrines are forbidden; honor God alone (Exod 20:3-5; Deut 12:2-4).

items.text: Before going forth, announce your purpose at the shrines of your grandfather and father with gifts; on the march place offerings of food by those gifts, and on returning announce again and bury the gifts between the steps leading to the high ancestor's fane.
items.quote: With gifts ... announce his purpose at the shrines of his grandfather and father. ... At every stage, he would place offerings of food by them.
items.conflict: Only God is to be worshiped; ancestor rites are idolatry (Exod 20:3-5; Lev 19:26-31).
